blocks.heading: 4 Transaction Advisory As a Side Door

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: The honest trade-off: Big 4 TAS analyst pay (roughly Rs 6-12 LPA) sits meaningfully below front-office IB pay, and the work is deal-adjacent (financial due diligence, valuation reports) rather than deal-leading (running the process, pitching clients directly). Treat this route as a 2-4 year on-ramp with an explicit lateral plan, not a comfortable long-term destination in itself.

supporting: Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and PwC all run Transaction Advisory Services (TAS) teams doing financial due diligence, valuation, and deal advisory work. EY's TAS practice in particular has been described by people who worked there as "as front-end IB as it gets," with colleagues who previously worked at boutique and bulge-bracket banks. Big 4 experience, especially inside TAS rather than audit, is a legitimate and commonly used path into IB, and banks hire laterals from these teams regularly.

blocks.heading: Skills You Actually Need Before You Apply

items.text: A structured financial modelling course (commonly Rs 20,000 to over Rs 1 lakh in India, depending on depth and placement support) can teach the mechanics faster than self-teaching from scratch, but the course certificate itself proves nothing to an interviewer.

supporting: A structured financial modelling course (commonly Rs 20,000 to over Rs 1 lakh in India, depending on depth and placement support) can teach the mechanics faster than self-teaching from scratch, but the course certificate itself proves nothing to an interviewer. The models you can build and explain afterward are what actually get checked. An unpaid or stipend-only internship at a boutique firm or a Big 4 valuation desk, even a short one, often teaches more real modelling judgment than a full course, because you are correcting real mistakes on a real client file instead of a practice template.

supporting: Can your body and sleep pattern genuinely handle 10am-to-2am days for stretches at a time, with weekend work during live deals, for at least the first 2 years? This is not a motivational question, it is a physical one, and India-specific attrition data shows a meaningful share of analysts leave in year one over exactly this.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Investment banking in India is frequently treated as a 2-3 year credential-building stop rather than a 30-year career, and that is not a weakness of the path, it is part of the design most analysts plan around. Common next moves include private equity (the classic exit, though India's PE ecosystem is smaller and more concentrated than in the US or UK), corporate development or finance roles inside large companies, an MBA if you did not already do one, or moving to a larger fund or bank if you started at a boutique or domestic firm.

visuals.heading: Not At a Top IIM

items.text: Pick your lane early: decide between the CA-to-IB lateral, the CFA-plus-portfolio route, or Big 4 transaction advisory based on your current degree, funding, and timeline, not on which sounds most prestigious.
Start the modelling portfolio immediately, in parallel: do not wait until you qualify as a CA or clear CFA Level 2 to build your first 3-statement model and DCF.
Target the on-ramp role deliberately: inside Big 4, aim specifically for transaction advisory, valuation, or deal advisory teams, not audit-only tracks.

Set a lateral step at 2-3 years: if you are still doing only routine advisory or audit work with no deal exposure by then, actively push for a transfer or start applying externally rather than waiting for the role to evolve on its own.
Get outside validation before every real application: show your model and pitch to someone already working in IB and use their feedback to close gaps before a real interview is on the line.
Build AI-tool fluency as a stated skill, not a hidden one: be ready to talk in an interview about how you use AI for first-draft modelling or research and how you check it for errors.
